cards.text: Paul, the apostle, is on the move again with a crew of companions, and the writer of Acts is one of them. The crew boards a ship and sails ahead to Assos to pick Paul up there. But Paul has arranged his own way to get to Assos.

cards.question: The crew sails to Assos to take Paul aboard there. How is Paul getting to Assos?

answers.text: He rides there on a donkey
He sails there on another ship

cards.text: Paul meets them at Assos, climbs aboard, and off they go: Mitylene, across from Chios, Samos, then Miletus. Friend, that's a LOT of islands for a man who just WALKED to the boat.

cards.question: Paul decides to sail right past Ephesus so he won't spend time in the province of Asia. Why is he in such a hurry?
Since Paul is sailing past Ephesus, he leaves without seeing anyone from the church there.
From Miletus, Paul sends to Ephesus for the ___ of the church.

cards.text: The elders come to Miletus, and Paul reminds them they know how he lived the whole time he was with them. He served the Lord with great humility and with tears.

cards.question: Paul says trials came on him while he was with the Ephesians. Where did those trials come from?

cards.text: And Paul says he held NOTHING back. If it was helpful to them, he taught it, no "let's circle back on that next quarter."

cards.question: Paul taught the Ephesians everything that was helpful. Where did he teach them?

answers.text: Publicly and from house to house

cards.question: Paul says he testified about repentance to God and faith in Jesus to the Jews, but not to the Greeks.

cards.text: Then Paul turns to what's ahead. Compelled by the Spirit, he's going to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to him there.

cards.question: Paul doesn't know what Jerusalem holds. But in town after town, what does the Holy Spirit warn him is waiting?
Chains and afflictions are waiting for Paul. So what does he say matters more to him than his own life?

answers.text: Finishing the ministry Jesus gave him
Seeing his friends one more time

cards.question: Paul tells the Ephesian elders he'll come back and see them again after Jerusalem.

cards.text: Paul says he's innocent of the blood of all men, because he never shrank back from declaring the whole will of God to them. Now the job passes to the elders: keep watch over themselves and the entire flock the Holy Spirit made them overseers of.

cards.question: The elders are overseers of the flock. So Paul tells them to be ___ of the church of God.

cards.text: This is the church God purchased with His own blood, Paul says. And he knows something is coming after he departs.

cards.question: Paul has been calling the church a flock. What does he warn will come in among them and not spare the flock?
Paul says the danger will only come from outside, never from the elders' own number.

cards.text: So be alert, Paul says, and remember that for three years he never stopped warning each of them, night and day, with tears. That is NOT a man who sent one reminder text and called it a day.

cards.question: Paul is about to leave the Ephesian elders. Who does he commit them to?

answers.text: God and the word of His grace

cards.text: Paul says he never coveted anyone's silver or gold or clothing. Me? I have stared at somebody else's batch of chocolate chip cookies a LITTLE too long, friend.

cards.question: Paul says these ___ of his took care of his own needs and the needs of his companions.
Paul says hard work like his is how we must help the weak. Which words of the Lord Jesus does he remember?

answers.text: It is more blessed to give than to receive
The worker is worthy of his wages
Ask and it will be given to you

cards.text: When Paul has said all this, he kneels down with every one of them.

cards.question: Paul is on his knees with the Ephesian elders. What does he do?
The elders say a quick goodbye to Paul and hold back their tears.
The elders weep as they embrace Paul. What grieves them most of all?

cards.text: Then they walk him all the way to the ship, and friend, I never got a goodbye like that. But Paul's road isn't done yet, so stick around.

findings.problem: The passage starts in the middle of the journey. Verse 13 says 'We went on ahead,' which only makes sense from Troas, the scene just before. The opening card says Paul is 'on the move again' but never says where the crew is leaving from, so the baker doesn't know where 'ahead' starts.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The joke calls the stops 'a LOT of islands,' but the text doesn't call them islands. Miletus, the last stop, is a mainland port, and the text has the ship only 'opposite Chios.' The joke also doesn't land: walking to Assos and then sailing past several places has no shared action to make the comparison click.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The joke logic fails. Walking to the boat isn't the same action as sailing past many stops, so the punchline needs explaining to make sense.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: The answer is False because the elders come and meet Paul, and that meeting happens in Acts 20:18 ('When they came to him'). Verse 17 only says Paul sent for them. The card cites only Acts 20:17, so the citation doesn't cover its right answer.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: The story card just before it says Paul 'held NOTHING back,' which rules out both wrong answers because each one starts with 'Only.' The right answer is also the only inclusive one and is longer, so it stands out from the other two.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question says 'The elders are overseers of the flock. So Paul tells them to be ___,' which presents the overseer role as Paul's reason for the command. Verse 28 says both things side by side and doesn't link them with a 'so.'

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'God and the word of His grace,' sounds like the Bible. The wrong answer 'Their own good judgment' sounds modern. In a Bible lesson, 'God' is the obvious pick even without the passage.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Most story cards are plain retelling with no voice, including stop 2 cards 1, 6, 10 and 12 and stop 3 card 1. Only a few cards carry jokes, and the stop 1 card 3 joke doesn't land. Overall, Papa Dorin reads like a pleasant narrator, not laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
